lessons.title: The honor you were born with
lessons.intro: What Allah says about your worth, and what to do when the world tells you otherwise.

steps.title: Who decides what you are worth?
body: Likes, grades, sizes, followers: all day, something is telling you what you are worth. Most of it changes every week.

In this lesson you will hear what Allah says about your worth, a worth you were given before you did anything. You will read two ayat, one hadith, and finish with a short thing to say when you feel small.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Honoured by Allah
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says He honoured the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, provided good things for them, and preferred them over much of His creation. This is said about all people, not only about the good ones.

steps.title: Hear the ayah
steps.note: Listen, then say it after the reciter in the pause.

steps.title: The best of stature
body: Allah swears that He created the human being in the best of stature (95:4). Elsewhere He tells the angels that when He had shaped Adam and breathed into him of His created soul, they were to prostrate to him (15:29).
Scholars explain that this honour is part of how people were made: the mind, the ability to speak, to choose, and to know their Lord. You did not earn it, and you cannot lose it by failing an exam.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Two kinds of honour
steps.intro: Scholars often separate the honour that comes with being human from the honour of nearness to Allah. The sentence below is a way of explaining the two ayat, not a quotation.
steps.agree: Everyone is honoured, and nearness to Allah is a matter of the heart.

rows.name: The honour you are born with
rows.text: Every human being is honoured by Allah in how they were made (17:70). Nobody can take it away, and no one has more of it than another.

rows.name: The honour you can grow
rows.text: The ayah of 49:13 says the most honourable in the sight of Allah is the most conscious of Him. This one is about taqwa, and it can grow or fade.

rows.name: What does not count
rows.text: Looks, wealth, tribe and followers. Muslim 2564 says Allah does not look at your faces and wealth, but at your hearts and deeds.

steps.closing: Start from your honour; grow your nearness.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The two-kinds-of-honour framing is a teaching summary, not a classical quotation. Please confirm the wording.

steps.title: The most noble of you
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah made people into peoples and tribes so that they would know one another. The most noble in His sight is the most righteous. Not the richest, the tallest or the most popular.

steps.title: What Allah looks at
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah does not look at your faces and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds (Muslim 2564).
A like count looks at your face. This hadith says Allah looks at something a camera cannot see.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: When you feel small
steps.intro: This is a short routine to say it to yourself, quietly, when the feed or the room makes you feel less.

steps.detail: Feeling small is a feeling. It is not a verdict.
Allah honoured the children of Adam (17:70). That includes me.

steps.text: Ask: what is Allah looking at?
steps.detail: My heart and my deeds (Muslim 2564). What is one small good deed I can do now?
Pray, call someone, give something, help someone.
It is a number, and it changes.

mistakes: Fixing your worth to a number.
Hiding it and telling nobody.
Thinking honour means you cannot make mistakes.
steps.label: [Reflection]

items.q: Who gives a person their basic honour, according to 17:70?

options.reteach: No. 17:70 says Allah honoured the children of Adam.
No. The honour is from Allah, before any of these.

items.q: What does 95:4 say Allah created the human being in?

options.reteach: No. 95:4 says the best of stature.
No. The ayah says the best of stature.

items.q: According to 49:13, who is the most noble in the sight of Allah?

options.text: The one from the largest tribe
options.reteach: No. 49:13 says the most righteous.
No. It says the most righteous.

items.q: What is the best response?

options.text: Remember that Allah looks at the heart and deeds, then do one good deed

options.reteach: A big reaction is not what the hadith says. It names hearts and deeds.

options.text: Post something to get more likes
options.reteach: That chases the number again.

items.scenario: Sara posted a photo and it got few likes. She feels worthless.

steps.prompt: Put the routine for feeling small in order.

items.text: Say what you know about your honour
Ask what Allah is looking at

steps.explain: Breathe, remember your honour, ask what Allah looks at, do a good deed, and leave the comparison.

steps.prompt: Match each text to what it teaches. Tap one on the left, then its meaning on the right.

right.text: Allah honoured the children of Adam

pairs.why: It is the ayah of the born-with honour.

right.text: Created in the best of stature

pairs.why: It speaks of how we were made.

right.text: The most noble is the most righteous

pairs.why: It is the honour you can grow.

right.text: Allah looks at hearts and deeds

pairs.why: It is the hadith about not judging by faces and wealth.

items.q: Which of these is honour you are born with?

options.text: The honour of a high score
options.reteach: A score can change. The honour in 17:70 is from Allah.

options.text: The honour of being a human being, given by Allah
The honour of a famous family
options.reteach: No. 49:13 says it is not about tribe.

items.q: What can you do to grow the honour of 49:13?

options.reteach: No. It is the most righteous.

options.text: Grow in taqwa, being conscious of Allah

options.reteach: No. It is about righteousness.

items.q: A hadith says Allah does not look at which two things?

options.reteach: No. He looks at your hearts and deeds.
These are what He does look at.

items.q: The lesson says the two-kinds-of-honour framing is...

options.text: A teaching summary, not a classical quotation

options.reteach: It is not a hadith. It is a summary of the two ayat.
It is not a ruling.

steps.title: Read the ayah
steps.body: Open Surah Al-Isra and read ayah 70. Then write one honest sentence: Allah honoured me, and one good deed I can do today is...

steps.title: What you can now do
canDo: Say who gave you your first honour, and name the ayah.
Say what 49:13 says about being noble.
Say what Allah looks at, according to Muslim 2564.
Use the routine for feeling small.

lessons.title: Chosen — Adam’s answer
lessons.intro: The story of the angels’ question, what Adam was taught, and the way back when you slip.

steps.title: Before you, there was a question
body: When Allah announced that He would place a successor on earth, the angels asked a hard question. The answer to that question is part of who you are.

This lesson follows the story of Adam in the Qur’an: the question of the angels, what Allah taught Adam, and what happened when he slipped. It ends with something practical for the days when you slip too.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The question of the angels
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah said He would make a successor on the earth. The angels asked whether He would place on it one who causes corruption and sheds blood, while they declare His praise. Allah answered: I know that which you do not know.

steps.title: Hear the ayah
steps.note: Listen to how the question and the answer are recited.

steps.title: What Adam was taught
body: Allah taught Adam the names, all of them. He showed them to the angels and asked them to tell Him the names. They said that they had no knowledge except what He taught them. Then Adam told them the names (2:31-33).
The scholars understand this as knowledge being part of what makes people able to carry responsibility on earth. You are not on earth by accident, and your mind is not a small thing.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The explanation that the names show knowledge as the basis of the human role is a common tafsir summary; please confirm the attribution.

steps.title: Adam slips and returns
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: After Adam and his wife ate from the tree they had been told to avoid, they said: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers. Allah accepted their repentance (2:37).

steps.title: Allah accepted him
body: The Qur’an says that Adam received words from his Lord, and Allah accepted his repentance, for He is the one who accepts repentance, the Merciful (2:37).

Notice what the Qur’an does not say. It does not say that Adam stayed in shame. The first human being made a mistake and came back, and that return is part of the story we were given. We are told it so that we know that coming back is open to us as well.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Do not despair
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah calls to those who have wronged themselves: do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Allah forgives all sins. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

steps.title: The question and the answer
steps.intro: The legacy lesson said your purpose is what the angels could not see. This is a short reading of the ayah, not a quote.
steps.agree: Everyone agrees that the ayah gives people a role as successors on the earth.

rows.name: The question of the angels
rows.text: Will you place one who causes corruption and sheds blood? A fair worry: people can do harm.

rows.name: Allah’s answer
rows.text: I know that which you do not know. People can do harm, and people can also do great good, learn, repent, and return.

rows.name: For you
rows.text: You are not defined by your worst day. You were created with a purpose, and you can return when you slip.

steps.closing: Carry the role and come back when you fall.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The reading of Allah’s answer as a hopeful reply is a common reflection, not a specific tafsir citation. Please confirm.

steps.title: When you slip: a way back
steps.intro: This follows the example of Adam and the call of 39:53.

steps.text: Stop and admit it, to Allah.
steps.detail: Adam said: we have wronged ourselves (7:23).
Say the words of Adam in 7:23, or simply ask in your own language.
Allah forgives all sins (39:53).
Apologise, return what is owed, change what led to it.
Pray the next prayer on time. A small good step is enough.

mistakes: Staying away from prayer out of shame.
Telling yourself it is too late.
Repeating the sin and calling it fate.
steps.label: [Established]

items.q: What did Allah answer the angels in 2:30?

options.text: I know that which you do not know
You are right, they will fail
options.reteach: No. He said I know that which you do not know.
No. He answered with I know that which you do not know.

items.q: What did Adam and his wife say after they slipped?

options.reteach: No. They said we have wronged ourselves (7:23).
The ayah has them asking for forgiveness.

options.text: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves

items.q: What does 39:53 tell people who have wronged themselves?

options.text: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah

options.reteach: No. It tells them not to despair of Allah’s mercy.
No. It calls them now.

items.q: What is the right step?

options.text: Ask Allah for forgiveness, put right what you can, and pray the next prayer on time
Skip prayer until he feels clean
options.reteach: This is the opposite. Return, do not stay away.

options.text: Tell himself it does not matter
options.reteach: It matters, and so does mercy.

items.scenario: Bilal slipped badly last night. He feels ashamed and wants to skip the next prayer.

steps.prompt: Put the events in the order the Qur’an tells them.

items.text: Allah announces a successor on the earth
items.why: The story starts with the announcement (2:30).
They ask about corruption and bloodshed.
He shows them to the angels.

items.text: Adam slips and says: we have wronged ourselves

steps.explain: Announcement, question, names, slip, repentance accepted.

steps.prompt: Match each text to its message. Tap one on the left, then its meaning on the right.

right.text: A successor on earth, and a question

pairs.why: It is the start of the story.

right.text: Adam taught the names
The words of Adam asking forgiveness
Do not despair of mercy

pairs.why: It is a call to those who sinned.

items.q: What does 2:37 say Allah did for Adam?

options.text: He sent him away with no hope
options.reteach: No. He accepted his repentance.
No. He accepted it.

items.q: What did the angels say they knew?

options.reteach: No. They said they had no knowledge except what He taught them (2:32).
They said they had no knowledge except what He taught them.

items.q: The lesson says the reading of the answer as hopeful is...

options.reteach: It is not a hadith.

options.text: A common reflection, flagged for scholar review

options.reteach: It is a reflection, not a ruling.

items.q: What is a good thing to say to a friend who thinks it is too late?

options.text: Allah forgives all sins; do not despair of His mercy
You are right, it is too late
options.reteach: No. 39:53 says do not despair.
Return to Allah rather than ignoring it.

items.scenario: A friend says he has sinned too much and it is too late to return.

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body: Open Surah Al-Baqarah and read ayat 30 to 37, or Al-A’raf 23. Then name one thing you can do that could serve others.

steps.title: What you can now do
canDo: Retell the question of the angels and Allah’s answer.
Say what Adam said after he slipped.
Say what 39:53 tells people who have sinned.
Give the steps of a way back.

lessons.title: Carrying the faith forward
lessons.intro: What the Prophet ﷺ said about the generations, about those who come later, and about passing on what you know.

steps.title: Born too late?
body: Some people feel the best days of Islam are over: the Prophet ﷺ and his companions were the real thing, and we are just what is left. Others feel the opposite, that they are the generation that will fix everything.
This lesson looks at what the Prophet ﷺ actually said about the generations, the one hadith about those who come later, and what you are asked to carry.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: What he said about the generations
body: Abdullah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: the people of my generation are the best, then those who follow them, then those who follow the latter (Bukhari 2652).

So the hadith does not say that we are the best generation. It says the first ones were. That is not a reason to give up. It is a reason to learn from them, to study how they lived, and to ask Allah to make us follow them.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: My brothers who have not come yet
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the graveyard and said: peace be upon you, abode of the believers. He added that he would love to see his brothers. The Companions asked: are we not your brothers? He said: you are my companions; our brothers are those who have not yet come into the world.
Think about that. The Prophet ﷺ spoke of people who would believe in him without having seen him, and called them his brothers. That includes believers today.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Strange, and glad tidings
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: Islam began as something strange and it will return to being strange, so glad tidings for the strangers (Muslim 145).

Some people hear this and feel alone. Read it again: it ends with glad tidings. If holding to your faith feels unusual at your school or your work, this hadith tells you it has happened before, and that the ones who hold on are praised.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Your job: convey
body: Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: convey from me even if it is a single sentence (Bukhari 3461).
You do not need to be a scholar to pass on a good thing you truly know. You do need to be careful: pass on only what you know to be true, and say when you do not know.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Youths who believed
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah tells the story of the People of the Cave: they were youths who believed in their Lord, and He increased them in guidance. It is one of the first stories the Qur’an tells about young people holding to their faith.

steps.title: A young man called Ibrahim
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: When Ibrahim spoke against the idols, the people said: we heard a young man mention them, who is called Ibrahim. The Qur’an remembers him as a young man who spoke up.

steps.title: One sunnah to practise this week
steps.intro: You do not need to do all. Choose one and keep it.

steps.detail: Something small and clear: saying Bismillah, greeting with salam, sitting to eat, sleeping on your right side.
Find the hadith. Ask your teacher if you are not sure.

steps.text: Do it without making a show.
steps.detail: You are not on a stage.
This is how you convey a single sentence.
Then add another.

mistakes: Doing it to impress.
Lecturing your friends.
Passing on something you are not sure of.
steps.label: [Reflection]

items.q: What does Bukhari 2652 say about the generations?

options.text: The people of his generation are the best, then those who follow them, then those who follow the latter
The last generation is the best
options.reteach: No. The hadith names the first generations as best.
No. The hadith ranks them.

items.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ call the believers who would come after him?

options.reteach: No. He said: you are my companions, and our brothers are those who have not yet come.
He used the word brothers.

items.q: What does Muslim 145 say about the strangers?

options.reteach: No. It says glad tidings for the strangers.
No. The hadith praises them.

items.q: A friend at school asks why you do not eat before saying Bismillah. What is a good answer?

options.text: Answer simply and kindly, and only share what you know to be true
Lecture him about it for an hour
options.reteach: The hadith says to convey, not to lecture.

options.text: Make up an answer so you do not look unsure
options.reteach: Do not say what you do not know. Say you will check.

items.scenario: A classmate notices you say Bismillah and asks why.

steps.prompt: Put these in order, from the first to the later.

items.text: The Prophet ﷺ and his generation
Believers who come later, including today
items.why: The Prophet ﷺ called them his brothers (Muslim 249).

steps.explain: The order of Bukhari 2652, and then the later believers of Muslim 249.

steps.prompt: Match each text to its meaning. Tap one on the left, then its meaning on the right.

right.text: The first generations are the best
Believers who come later are his brothers

pairs.why: It comforts those who never saw him.

right.text: Glad tidings for the strangers

pairs.why: It is for those who hold on when it feels unusual.

right.text: Convey even one sentence

pairs.why: It is your job to pass on what you know.

items.q: Why is it wrong to say the hadith calls our generation the best?

options.text: Because it does not mention generations
options.reteach: It does mention them.

options.text: Because Bukhari 2652 names the early generations as best
Because only the Prophet ﷺ was the best
options.reteach: The hadith speaks about generations.

items.q: Who were the People of the Cave, according to 18:13?

options.reteach: No. The ayah says youths.

options.text: Youths who believed in their Lord

options.reteach: No. They were youths.

items.q: What does the lesson ask you to be careful about when you convey?

options.text: To pass on everything you hear
options.reteach: No. Pass on what you know to be true.

options.text: To pass on only what you know to be true, and to say when you do not know

options.reteach: The hadith says to convey.

items.q: What is the right feeling for a believer who holds on when it feels unusual?

options.text: Hope, because the hadith ends with glad tidings

options.reteach: No. Muslim 145 says glad tidings.
It is hope, not pride.

steps.title: Read the youths of the cave
steps.body: Open Surah Al-Kahf and read ayat 9 to 16. It tells how young people held to their faith.

steps.title: What you can now do
canDo: Say what Bukhari 2652 says and what it does not say.
Say whom the Prophet ﷺ called his brothers.
Say what Muslim 145 tells the strangers.
Name one sunnah you will practise this week.
steps.next: Next: The scroll that eats the hour.

lessons.title: The scroll that eats the hour
lessons.intro: Time as a blessing, what Surah Al-Asr teaches, and one small limit you can keep.

steps.title: Where did the hour go?
body: You pick up the phone for a minute. Then it is an hour. Nothing bad happened, and nothing good did either. Most of us know this feeling.

This lesson is about time. You will read the short surah about time, a hadith about a blessing most people lose, and plan one small limit that you can keep. It is about your phone, but it applies to any screen.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: By time
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah swears by time, and says that mankind is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds, and advise each other to truth and to patience. Time is the field of this loss, and the way out is faith, good deeds, and good company.

steps.title: Hear Surah Al-Asr
steps.note: Listen to the last ayah. Notice the words for truth and patience.

steps.title: The blessing most people lose
body: Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: there are two blessings that many people lose by being careless with them: health and free time (Bukhari 6412).
Free time is a blessing from Allah. The scroll does not announce that it is taking it. It just takes a minute, and then another.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What distracts from remembrance
body: Allah says: do not let your wealth and your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah; whoever does that, they are the losers (63:9). The ayah names wealth and children, which are good things. A good thing can still push out remembrance when it takes too much of you.
A phone is not named in the ayah. The lesson applies the idea: when anything, even a good thing, pushes out remembrance and prayer, it is time to put it back in its place.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The application of 63:9 to phones is a reflection; the ayah itself names wealth and children. Please confirm.

steps.title: Five anchors
body: The Prophet ﷺ said: if there were a river at the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain on him? They said no. He said: that is the example of the five prayers; Allah wipes away sins through them (Bukhari 528).
Five prayers cut the day into five parts. If you let the prayer call you away from the screen, the day has a shape that the feed cannot give it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Turn away from idle talk
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: One quality of the believers in Surah Al-Mu’minun is that they turn away from idle talk. This is not about being boring. It is about not letting empty noise fill the day.

steps.title: Set one limit you can keep
steps.intro: Choose one of these. Small and kept is better than big and broken.

steps.detail: Look at your screen time for yesterday. Do not judge, just look.
No phone at meals, or none in the bedroom, or none in the first ten minutes after Fajr.
Charge the phone in another room. Turn off notifications you do not need.
Put something in its place: a walk, a call, a few ayat.
Ask a friend or family member to do it with you.

mistakes: Deleting everything at once and going back after two days.
Making it a punishment.
Telling yourself it is only a minute.
steps.label: [Reflection]

items.q: In Surah Al-Asr, who is not in loss?

options.text: Those who believe, do righteous deeds, and advise each other to truth and patience

options.reteach: No. 103:3 names the believers who do good and advise each other.
No. They advise each other, so they are with people.

items.q: What are the two blessings many people lose, in Bukhari 6412?

options.reteach: No. The hadith says health and free time.
No. It is health and free time.

items.q: What does the lesson say about applying 63:9 to phones?

options.text: It is a reflection; the ayah itself names wealth and children

options.reteach: It does not. It names wealth and children.

options.text: It has nothing to do with it
options.reteach: It is an application of the idea, not the wording.

items.q: What is a good first limit?

options.text: Charge the phone in another room at night
Delete every app today and never reinstall
options.reteach: That is too big to keep. Small and kept is better.

options.text: Check it more often to see what you miss
options.reteach: That is the opposite of a limit.

items.scenario: Adam wakes up and scrolls for forty minutes before Fajr is over.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of setting a limit in order.

items.why: For example, no phone at meals.
Charge it elsewhere. Turn off notifications.
A walk, a call, a few ayat.

steps.explain: Notice, pick, make easy, replace, tell someone.

steps.prompt: Match each text to its message. Tap one on the left, then its meaning on the right.

right.text: Time is a field of loss and gain

pairs.why: It names the way out of loss.

right.text: Health and free time are blessings
Do not be distracted from remembrance
The five prayers as a river

items.q: What does the river example in Bukhari 528 teach?

options.reteach: No. The hadith uses the river as an example of the prayers.

options.text: The five prayers wipe away sins, like bathing five times a day
You only need to pray once
options.reteach: No. It speaks of five times.

items.q: Which is a replace, not just remove, action?

options.text: Delete the phone and sit in silence
options.reteach: Replace the habit with something good, not just silence.

options.text: Phone away at meals, and talk with the family

options.reteach: That is not a limit.

items.q: What does 23:3 say believers turn away from?

options.reteach: No. It says idle talk.
No. It says idle talk.

items.q: A friend says one minute does not matter. What does Bukhari 6412 add?

options.text: Free time is a blessing, and many people lose it by being careless
He is right, minutes do not matter
options.reteach: The hadith treats free time as a blessing.
The hadith speaks of free time itself.

steps.title: Pray on time, phone away
steps.body: Open prayer times and make the next prayer a phone-free one: put the phone in another room before you begin.

steps.title: What you can now do
canDo: Say what Surah Al-Asr says about time and loss.
Name the two blessings of Bukhari 6412.
Explain why the lesson calls 63:9 and phones a reflection.
Set one limit you can keep.
steps.next: Next: The feed is not real.

lessons.title: The feed is not real
lessons.intro: Why the feed makes you feel small, what the Prophet ﷺ said about looking up and looking down, and how to clean up.

steps.title: Everyone else looks fine
body: You see their holiday, their grades, their friends. You do not see their night. Of course it feels like everyone is doing better than you.

This lesson is about comparing yourself to what you see online. You will read what the Prophet ﷺ said about looking at those above and below you, an ayah about what we should not wish for, and a short plan for cleaning up your feed.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: What counts with Allah
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah does not look at your faces and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds (Muslim 2564).
The feed shows faces and wealth. Allah looks at something else. So when the feed makes you feel small, remember that it is measuring the wrong thing.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Look at who is below you
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: when one of you looks at someone who is above him in wealth and appearance, let him also look at someone who is below him (Bukhari 6490). In Muslim 2963 he added that this is better, so that you do not look down on the favours of Allah.
This is not about feeling superior. It is about balance. If you only look up, you will always feel poor, and you will forget what you have been given.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Do not wish for what others have
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says: do not wish for that by which Allah has favoured some of you over others. Each has a share of what they have earned. Ask Allah of His bounty. It is a calm ayah, and it answers envy with a du’a, not with a fight.

steps.title: Do not ridicule
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: The same feed that makes you feel small can make you cruel. 49:11 says do not let a people ridicule another people, perhaps they are better than them, and do not call each other by bad nicknames.

steps.title: Suspicion and spying

Much of the feed is built on looking for faults and wondering about people. This hadith asks us to stop at the first step.

lessons.title: Guarding the gaze
lessons.intro: What the Qur’an and the Prophet ﷺ taught about the gaze, and practical steps for the screen.

steps.title: The easiest sin
body: The gaze used to need a street. Now it needs a thumb. The ayah about lowering the gaze is old, but the test is new.

This lesson explains what the Qur’an and the Prophet ﷺ said about the gaze, for both young men and young women, with simple steps for the screen. It is written without shame: everyone struggles with this.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The command to the men
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says: tell the believing men to reduce some of their vision and guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Allah is acquainted with what they do.

steps.title: And to the women
body: The next ayah gives the same instruction to believing women: to reduce some of their vision and guard their private parts (24:31). The command is for both, and the Qur’an addresses them in the same words at the start.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The sudden glance
body: Jarir ibn Abdullah said that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the sudden glance. The Prophet ﷺ commanded him to turn away his eyes (Muslim 2159).
The first look that you did not choose is not the problem. What matters is what you do next: turn away, or keep looking.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The eye will be asked
body: Allah says: do not follow that of which you have no knowledge. Hearing, sight and the heart will each be questioned (17:36).
This includes what we watch. It is one of the reasons that scholars connect lowering the gaze to guarding the heart.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Where scholars say there is room
steps.intro: The rule is general, and scholars discuss exceptions. This is only a short note.
steps.agree: The command to lower the gaze is for everyone.

rows.name: The rule
rows.text: Both men and women are told to reduce some of their vision (24:30-31).

rows.name: Looking with a need
rows.text: Scholars discuss cases such as treatment by a doctor, looking at someone you intend to propose to, or a witness in court. The details differ by school.

rows.name: What this means for you
rows.text: If you are not sure whether a situation is allowed, ask a qualified teacher. Do not rely on a search result.

steps.closing: Start with the rule, and ask about the cases.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the summary of exceptions (doctor, proposal, witness) and that the details differ by school.

steps.title: Another route the Prophet ﷺ gave
body: Ibn Mas’ud reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: young men, whoever of you can marry, should marry, because it lowers the gaze and protects chastity; and whoever cannot, should fast, for it is a shield (Bukhari 5066).
This is not a command to marry before you are ready. It shows that the Prophet ﷺ treated the gaze as a real need, and gave real answers: marriage when able, and fasting when not.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Practical steps for the screen
steps.intro: None of these is a fatwa. They are tools that many people find helpful.

steps.detail: When something comes up, close it, look elsewhere.
Do not scroll alone in the dark; keep devices out of the bedroom.
Ask Allah for help. It is part of the answer.
Pray two rak’ahs, walk, call a friend.
If you slip, make tawbah and start again (Qur’an 39:53).
Talk to a trusted older person or counsellor if it is becoming a habit.

mistakes: Staying alone with it.
Leaving the prayer out of shame.
Blaming only the other person.
steps.label: [Reflection]

lessons.title: Choose your company
lessons.intro: What the Qur’an and the Prophet ﷺ said about friends, and how to choose and be a good one.

steps.title: Who is in your circle?
body: You become a little like the people you spend time with. Most of us know it, and most of us do not choose on purpose.
This lesson uses one hadith, one picture from the Prophet ﷺ, and two ayat to help you choose your company, and to be a good friend yourself.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: On the religion of his friend
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: a man is upon the religion of his friend, so let one of you look at whom he befriends (Tirmidhi 2378 (graded hasan by al-Albani)).
It does not say a person is the same as his friend. It says he follows him, in habits, speech, and what he thinks is normal. So choose carefully.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The musk seller and the blacksmith
body: Abu Musa reported that the Prophet ﷺ gave this example: a good companion and an evil companion are like a person carrying musk and a person blowing a bellows. The musk carrier will either give you some, or you will buy some from him, or you will smell a good smell from him. The one blowing the bellows will either burn your clothes, or you will smell a bad smell (Bukhari 5534).
He does not tell you to cut off everyone who is not perfect. He tells you what each kind of company does to you.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The regret of the wrong friend
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: On the Day of Judgment, the wrongdoer will bite his hands and say: I wish I had taken a way with the Messenger. I wish I had not taken that one as a friend. He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me.

steps.title: Friends on that Day
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Close friends, on that Day, will be enemies to each other, except the righteous. A friendship built on good survives.

steps.title: Keep yourself with them
body: Allah tells His Messenger ﷺ to keep himself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face; and not to let his eyes pass over them, desiring the adornments of this life (18:28).
The ayah asks you to choose to sit with good people, even when others seem more exciting. Notice it says patient: it takes effort.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: How to choose and be a good friend
steps.intro: These are practical, in the spirit of the sources above.

steps.detail: Write the names down.

steps.text: Ask what each brings out in you.
steps.detail: Honesty? Prayer? Gossip? Laziness?

steps.text: Make room for a good one.
steps.detail: Join a halaqah, a masjid youth group, a sports team with good manners.
Remind kindly, give a gift, keep secrets, make du’a for them.

steps.text: Do not drop people in anger.
steps.detail: Spend less time if needed, but stay kind.

mistakes: Cutting everyone off.
Staying in a group that pulls you away from prayer because you fear being alone.
Giving advice with a sneer.
steps.label: [Reflection]

lessons.title: Halal money — even the penny
lessons.intro: Why the source of your money matters, the doubt test, and a simple check for a job or deal.

steps.title: Your first pay
body: A first job, pocket money, a side hustle, a gift: money comes into a young person’s hands for the first time. Where it came from matters as much as how much.

This lesson explains why the source of your money matters, the doubt test the Prophet ﷺ gave, and a hadith about the cost of mixing halal and haram. It gives a simple check you can use for a job or a deal.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Eat from the good things
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says: O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you, and be grateful to Allah if it is Him you worship. The good things (tayyibat) come with gratitude.

steps.title: Allah is good
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: O people, Allah is Good and accepts only what is good. Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dusty and dishevelled, raising his hands to the sky and saying: O Lord, O Lord, while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful and he was nourished by the unlawful; so how can his prayer be answered? (Muslim 1015).
The hadith lists everything that supports a person’s life, and ties it to du’a. It does not say a single wrong penny ruins a person. It says that earning matters to how we pray.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The doubt test
body: Al-Hasan ibn Ali remembered the Prophet ﷺ saying: leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt. The truth brings tranquility, and falsehood brings doubt (Tirmidhi 2518 (graded sahih by al-Albani)).
This gives you a quick test for a job or a deal. If something leaves you uneasy, ask someone who knows before you go ahead.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The clear and the doubtful
body: Nu’man ibn Bashir reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: the halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that most people do not know. Whoever avoids the doubtful matters has protected his religion and honour. Whoever falls into the doubtful is like a shepherd who grazes his flock around a protected pasture and is about to graze in it (Bukhari 52).
So there are three groups: clear halal, clear haram, and unclear. For the unclear ones, ask and be careful.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A time when people do not care
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: a time will come when people will not care whether what they earned was lawful or unlawful (Bukhari 2083).
This is a warning against being careless. It is easy to take a job or a deal because everyone does, without asking.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A simple check for a job or deal
steps.intro: This is a practical checklist. It does not replace asking a scholar.

steps.detail: What is the work or the deal, in plain words?
Is anyone cheated, lied to, or harmed?

steps.text: Ask if the thing itself is allowed.
steps.detail: Is the product or work something Islam forbids?
Does it leave you uneasy?
A trusted imam, teacher or parent. Bring the details.
If you leave something for His sake, trust that He will replace it with better.

mistakes: Taking it because everyone does.
Not asking because you fear the answer.
Hiding details when you ask.
steps.label: [Reflection]
steps.review: Please confirm that the last step, trusting that Allah replaces what is left for His sake, does not need a source; it is stated as a reflection.

lessons.title: Seven under the shade
lessons.intro: The hadith of the seven whom Allah will shade, and what you can start while you are young.

steps.title: What you can do only now
body: Some things are easiest when you are young: a fresh memory, plenty of energy, a clear schedule. Later they get harder.

This lesson reads one of the best-known hadith about young people, the list of seven whom Allah will shade, and asks what you can start now. It does not promise a result; it shows what the Prophet ﷺ praised.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Seven whom Allah will shade
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: Allah will shade seven on the Day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a youth who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two people who love each other for Allah’s sake, meeting and parting upon it; a man called by a woman of rank and beauty who says: I fear Allah; a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right gives; and a man who remembers Allah in seclusion and his eyes overflow (Bukhari 660).
The second one is a young person. The hadith praises the youth who grew up in worship, not the one who waited until later.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Youths who believed
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: The Qur’an says of the People of the Cave that they were youths who believed in their Lord, and Allah increased them in guidance.

steps.title: I seek refuge in Allah
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Yusuf, a young man in a house where he was tempted, said: I seek the refuge of Allah. This is the response of the fifth person in the hadith, the one who is called and says: I fear Allah. Read the meaning of what he said.

steps.title: A strong believer
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not lose heart (Muslim 2664).
Strength here means more than the body. It is energy, time, and the will to learn that you can put to use for what benefits you.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Now and later
steps.intro: This is a reflection, not a ruling.
steps.agree: Every age has things that are easier for it.

rows.name: What is easier when you are young
rows.text: Memorising, learning a language, long nights, trying new habits, health.

rows.name: What is easier when you are older
rows.text: Some forms of charity, knowledge from experience, steady patience.

rows.name: A fair thought
rows.text: Neither is better. The aim is not to postpone what you can do now.

steps.closing: Do now what is easier now.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Thirty minutes this week
steps.intro: Choose one of these and put it in your diary.

steps.text: Choose one: memorise, pray at night, learn Arabic, or serve.
steps.detail: A small, specific plan: memorise five ayat, or pray two rak’ahs after Isha.
A fixed time and place.
Ten minutes is enough on day one.

steps.text: Do it for Allah, not for a show.
steps.detail: The hadith praises secret charity and private remembrance.
Seek help from Allah (Muslim 2664).

mistakes: Planning for hours and starting nothing.
Telling everyone and quitting quietly.
Looking down on people who are older.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Start with the Qur’an
steps.body: Open the Qur’an and read the first ayat of Surah Al-Kahf, which tells of the youths. Then write down one thing to start this week.

steps.title: What you can now do
canDo: Name at least five of the seven in Bukhari 660, including the youth.
Say what Yusuf said in 12:23.
Say what Muslim 2664 asks you to be keen on.
Pick one thing to do for thirty minutes this week.
steps.next: You have finished the Youth course.
